about: How a delivery looks (beenster, 9 Nov: cardboard for smaller parts, wooden crates for larger and heavier ones, a label from a made-up delivery firm, a coloured sticky note saying who it's for). The game (ATorqueShedItems, drawing a boxed item) picks the container by the part's kind, the variant nearest the box's shape (its size: TorqueShedItems KindSize + 8 cm) and scales it to that size; lays SM_courier_label flat on the lid (and one on the front for a crate) at its real 16 x 10 cm, its material's 'Courier' row from the item id (as bike_model.gd courier_for), and writes the contents and tracking number into the label's blank strip; and sticks SM_sticky_note on the front face, its 'Tint' the orderer's player colour, with 'For <name>' written on it. Couriers are Torque Shed's own (bike_model.gd COURIERS): made-up names, no real companies.
variant_sizes_note: cm as (long x, wide y, high z) in UE, the same order as KindSize. The meshes' own frame is Torque Shed's (x long, y up, z deep): the game maps x->x, z->y, y->z.

note.place: front face, upper left quarter, a few degrees off square
